title_en: The covenant and the mountain raised above them
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT record: it stays inside the event's own inventory refs, is shorter than the prophet story that also tells the event, and refers to that story only in general words. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims; passages from several surahs are grouped by theme and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it, so that they might be mindful.

Another passage says that He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them, and told them to take what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it.

A later verse repeats the taking of the covenant and the raising of the mountain, and says that they said they heard and disobeyed, and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief.
A further passage says that God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it [c1][c2]. Another passage adds that they were to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it, so that they might be mindful [c1]. Another passage says that He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them [c2].

A later verse repeats the taking of the covenant and the raising of the mountain, and says that they said they heard and disobeyed [c3]. A further passage says that God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The verses tell one scene from different sides: the covenant and the command [c1], the canopy and the fear that it would fall [c2], the answer they gave [c3], and the further commands of the gate and the Sabbath [c4]. The repeated reminder in the same surah is placed after a mention of the calf [c3]. Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these verses say you and them [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God took a promise from them and lifted the mountain above them [c1][c2]. God told them to hold on to what He gave them and to remember what is in it [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the covenant is joined to a command to take what was given with strength and to remember it [c1]. Another is that the later verse records the answer they gave [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when this took place in relation to the tablets or the calf.
- Not established: the nature of the raising of the mountain; interpreters differ on whether it is to be taken literally.
- Not established: what the gate and the Sabbath refer to in 4:154.
- Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these verses say you and them and do not name the people in this record.
- The relation between 2:63 and 2:93, a repeated reminder in the same surah, is a matter for scholars.
- The inventory also treats these verses as one event; the verses themselves do not say that the passages are one scene (an inference).

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about the raising of the mountain. None is used in this draft.
The event is also told inside a chapter of the longer prophet story (content/stories/musa.draft.json); this record is a shorter account that refers to it only in general words.

The identification of those addressed in these verses with the people of the prophet's story is made from the surrounding passages and the event inventory, not from these verses alone; a scholar should confirm it.
The passages (2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171) are read as one scene on matching wording (an inference).
The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of the chapters is a reading order only.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
